summary.text: Thermal conduction is the spread of heat through a material, or between materials in contact, as particles pass their energy along.
Heat flows from hotter to colder, as when a stove burner warms the bottom of a pan, and the temperature difference fades over time.
Metals conduct well because free-moving electrons carry energy quickly, while liquids and gases, with sparser particles, conduct poorly.

facts.label: Direction of flow
facts.value: From the hotter body to the colder body

facts.label: Conductivity symbol
facts.value: Written k, it measures how easily a medium conducts

facts.label: Good conductors
facts.value: Metals such as copper, platinum and gold

items.prompt: You hold one end of a copper rod in a flame. Why does the far end warm up so quickly?

options.label: Hot air rises along the rod and heats it
Free-moving electrons carry thermal energy rapidly
Copper atoms travel from the flame to your hand
Light from the flame passes through the metal

items.explain: Metallic bonds have free-moving electrons that transfer thermal energy rapidly, which makes metals good conductors.

items.prompt: A hot pan sits flat on a cool counter. Which way does heat move, and what happens to the temperature difference?

options.label: Pan to counter, and the difference shrinks over time
Counter to pan, and the difference shrinks over time
Pan to counter, and the difference grows over time
Neither way, since solids never exchange heat

items.explain: Heat flows spontaneously from hotter to colder, and with nothing opposing it, temperature differences decay toward thermal equilibrium.

items.prompt: Why is a gas a poor conductor of heat?

options.label: Its particles are bonded too strongly to vibrate
Its particles all move in the same direction
Its particles are crowded so energy gets trapped
Its particles are far apart and collide rarely

items.explain: Gases have a lot of space between particles, so collisions are infrequent and vibrations are hard to pass along.

items.prompt: A metal bar has one end held hot and the other held cold for a long time. What is true of any section of the bar?

options.label: It loses more heat than it receives
It gains more heat than it gives up
It receives as much heat as it passes on
It keeps warming up until the bar melts

items.explain: In steady-state conduction the heat entering any region equals the heat leaving it; otherwise the temperature there would keep rising or falling.

items.prompt: Each of these warms something. Which one depends on direct physical contact?

options.label: Sunlight warming the Earth
A burner warming the bottom of a pan
A furnace blowing warm air through a house
Your body warming a person across the room

items.explain: Conduction is heat transfer by contact, as between a stove burner and a pan. The others are radiation or convection.

items.prompt: A solid has no free-moving electrons to speak of. What carries most of the heat through it?

options.label: Vibrations passing between its atoms
A drifting stream of electrons
Currents of the material flowing inside it
Heat rays crossing the gaps between atoms

items.explain: In insulators the heat flux is carried almost entirely by phonon vibrations, the vibrations of the atoms in the solid.
